title: Gulf of Maine temperature shock
region: Northeastern United States / Gulf of Maine
observation: In Holyoke’s Salem air-temperature series, daily average and low temperatures in 1816 were more than one standard deviation lower, while daily temperature differential was more than one standard deviation higher, than the other years in the 1814–1818 comparison.
uncertainty: Salem air-temperature observations provide regional context; these are not direct sea-temperature measurements or a Gulf-wide instrumental network.
sourceLocator: Alexander et al., results and temperature-series methods

title: Migratory fish populations respond
observation: Abnormal temperatures affected alewives, shad, herring and mackerel differently according to migration/spawning phenology and temperature tolerance; alewives were particularly affected.
uncertainty: Species responses are inferred from fisheries records, air temperatures and later phenological knowledge; direct fish behavior and mortality were not measured in 1816.

title: Food pressure shifts fishing effort
observation: Crop failure and threat of famine increased pressure on fisheries; insufficient alewife runs contributed to fishers shifting effort toward mackerel, making 1816 remembered as the 'mackerel year'.

title: Temporary shock produces structural fishery change
observation: The shift from riparian toward marine fisheries persisted and expanded after temperatures moderated and alewife populations recovered, indicating a lasting human-system adaptation after the short climate shock.

title: Extremely cold summer in the Czech Lands
observation: Instrumental and documentary evidence records an extremely cold summer in 1816; documentary evidence also records damaging weather and poor grain harvests.

title: Harvest losses become grain-price pressure
observation: Bad grain harvests associated with the 1815–1816 weather were followed by widespread grain-price increases culminating in 1817.

title: Persistent rain in southwestern Bohemia
observation: Václav Jan Mašek of Řenče reports rain beginning 8 June 1816 and continuing for about eight weeks with few rain-free days; wet cereals, poor yields, rising prices and hunger were reported.
uncertainty: Local documentary account; not a measured regional rainfall total.

title: Tambora eruption as an antecedent global shock
observation: The April 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora injected volcanic material into the atmosphere and is identified as a major contributor to the unusually cold 1816 summer in much of Europe and other Northern Hemisphere climate anomalies.

title: Geneva summer afternoons shift 3–4°C colder
observation: Compared with the 1799–1821 reference period, the distribution of afternoon summer temperature anomalies in Geneva shifted by roughly 3–4°C toward colder conditions; increased cloudiness contributed substantially to the pattern.

title: Exceptional Alpine snow storage
observation: Historical reports and hydrological reconstruction indicate substantial snow storage in 1816 and 1817; snowfall events reached unusually low elevations and snow conditions helped set up the hydrological sensitivity of 1817.

title: Lake Constance and Rhine flooding in 1817
place: Rhine at Basel and Lake Constance
observation: On 6–7 July 1817 major flooding affected the Rhine at Basel and Lake Constance; Lake Constance reached the highest documented flood level in the cited reconstruction. Snowmelt combined with intense rainfall was central to the event.

title: Southern China experiences unusual cold, frost and snow
observation: Tree-ring and Chinese documentary proxies show a Tambora-era cold excursion with severe frost damage and snow and ice accumulations unusual for southern China.
sourceLocator: Gao et al., Table 1 and section 3.1
uncertainty: Reported snow and ice include late 1815–January 1816; events are not all confined to calendar 1816.

title: China hydroclimate signal is spatially uneven
observation: Tree-ring drought reconstructions indicate drying tendencies consistent with weakened monsoonal circulation, while documentary drought and flood records show much milder responses outside southern China. The divergence is itself important evidence about proxy sensitivity and regional variation. A multiproxy precipitation reconstruction also lacks a strong response, reinforcing the disagreement across evidence systems.
uncertainty: Drying is not uniformly supported across regions or reconstruction methods.

title: Laennec invents the stethoscope
observation: René-Théophile-Hyacinthe Laennec developed mediate auscultation in 1816 by using a rolled paper tube to transmit chest sounds; he then spent several years refining the instrument and correlating clinical signs with pathology.

title: Frankenstein begins in the cold, stormy summer of 1816
observation: Mary Godwin conceived the story that became Frankenstein during the cold, rainy summer near Geneva; surviving Notebook A contains draft material written from August to early December 1816.

title: United Provinces declare independence
historicalEntity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
observation: On 9 July 1816 the Congress of Tucumán declared the formal break of the United Provinces from the Spanish monarchy; the declaration formed part of the wider Spanish American independence process.

title: Treaty of Sugauli ratified
historicalEntity: Kingdom of Nepal / East India Company
observation: The Treaty of Sugauli was exchanged/ratified on 4 March 1816 after the Anglo-Nepalese War. Its articles recognized territorial cessions to the East India Company and provided for accredited ministers between the two states.

title: Anglo-Dutch fleet bombards Algiers
observation: An Anglo-Dutch fleet under Edward Pellew bombarded Algiers on 27 August 1816 after demands for the release of captives were not met. Royal Museums Greenwich records that 1,083 Christian slaves and the British consul were subsequently liberated and restitution and peace terms secured.

title: Shaka assumes AmaZulu chieftaincy and begins expansion
observation: Following the death of Senzangakhona in 1816, Shaka returned and took the AmaZulu chieftaincy. Scholarly chronology describes campaigns and incorporation of nearby chiefdoms during 1816–1817 as part of an expanding political formation.

title: Slachter’s Nek rebels executed
observation: Five men convicted after the 1815 Slachter’s Nek rebellion were publicly hanged on 9 March 1816. The episode later acquired substantial political memory among Afrikaners, though interpretations of its longer-term causal importance differ.

title: The Barber of Seville premieres
observation: Rossini's Il Barbiere di Siviglia premiered at Rome's Teatro Argentina on 20 February 1816. Its opening night was poorly received, but a revised Bologna performance in August was highly successful, preceding rapid wider diffusion.

title: Ashfall devastates Sumbawa croplands
observation: Heavy tephra fall devastated croplands around Tambora; pyroclastic flows reached the sea on the Sanggar Peninsula.
uncertainty: Spatial damage is summarized; no district yield series is available here.

title: Famine and disease follow the local eruption
topic: Famine and disease follow the local eruption
observation: Reports and later scholarship describe starvation and disease after the eruption on Sumbawa and neighboring islands.
uncertainty: Approximate 1815 aftermath; persistence into 1816 is unresolved. No independently measured annual mortality total is supplied.

title: Rice relief and distress livestock sales on Sumbawa
historicalEntity: Sumbawa island polities / British administration in Java
topic: Rice relief and distress livestock sales on Sumbawa
evidenceType: Contemporary documentary report via scholarly review
observation: A report reproduced in scholarship describes people exchanging livestock for small amounts of staples and an official rice gift to the ruler of Sanggar.
uncertainty: Approximate 1815 aftermath; day and month not established here. Colonial report offers a local snapshot; wider relief effectiveness is unresolved.
sourceLocator: Oppenheimer pp. 248–249; Philipps report via Raffles (1817, 1830)

title: Dry conditions reconstructed across monsoon Asia
topic: Dry conditions reconstructed across monsoon Asia
observation: The Monsoon Asia Drought Atlas reconstruction indicates dry conditions in India and Southeast Asia during May–September 1816.
uncertainty: Proxy reconstruction is spatially broad; it does not establish local rainfall totals, harvest losses or famine.
sourceLocator: p. 7, discussion of Monsoon Asia Drought Atlas

title: Macquarie orders punitive expeditions
historicalEntity: Dharawal, Dharug and Gandangara peoples / New South Wales colony
observation: Macquarie issued instructions for military expeditions against Aboriginal people, authorizing violence and hostage-taking.
uncertainty: Colonial records encode the administration’s viewpoint; orders and subsequent conduct must be distinguished.

title: Appin massacre
historicalEntity: Dharawal people / New South Wales colony
observation: Wallis’s detachment attacked a sleeping Aboriginal group near the Cataract River, killing men, women and children.
uncertainty: Official death toll of 14 is a minimum in the museum account; the full toll remains uncertain.
sourceLocator: Captain Wallis diary and museum comparison

title: Colonial proclamation restricts Aboriginal movement
historicalEntity: Aboriginal peoples / New South Wales colony
observation: A proclamation published in the Sydney Gazette restricted Aboriginal gatherings, movement and what people could carry.
uncertainty: Policy text establishes imposed rules; enforcement and local responses need separate records.

title: Army of the Andes command and training
historicalEntity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
topic: Army of the Andes command and training
observation: San Martín was appointed commander of the Army of the Andes in August; units entered the El Plumerillo training camp in September.
uncertainty: Chronology establishes preparation; supply volumes and labor contributions need additional sources.

title: Army crosses Andean passes
observation: Multiple columns departed Cuyo in January and crossed the Andes; the army assembled west of the mountains in February.
uncertainty: Date range includes several routes and departures rather than one crossing day.

title: Victory at Chacabuco
historicalEntity: Army of the Andes / Spanish royalist forces
observation: San Martín’s army defeated royalist forces commanded by Maroto at Chacabuco.
uncertainty: Victory alone does not establish the later independence outcome or explain all military causes.
